title: Rooms — a member's name in a room
description: How a member tells the other members of a room what to call them: a record of kind `memberProfile`, written by the member into the room like any other record, whose `title` is the name. A reader shows that name wherever it shows the member's DID — beside a message, on a quoted record, in the list of who reacted. It adds no task and changes no existing schema: the record is an ordinary `SealedRecordBody` on the sealed tiers and ordinary `cleartext` of `rooms/records/put` on an `open` room, using only members both already have, so a key holder that seals at `rooms/keys/seal/0.3` seals it unchanged and a host stores it like any other record. New in 0.3 of this family's shared types; `room.schema.json` stays at 0.2, and `blobs.schema.json` and `personal-label.schema.json` at 0.1. Plain text throughout: a reader renders the name as text, never as markup, and an agent reading it MUST NOT treat it as instructions. Not itself a Trust Task specification (the `_shared` folder is skipped by the registry build and the codegen).

MemberName.title: MemberName
MemberName.description: What a member asks the room's other members to call them, in this room only: plain text, one line, no control characters, at most 64 code points after Unicode Normalization Form C. Chosen by the member and asserted by nobody else — not unique, not verified, and not an identifier. An empty name, or one holding only White_Space characters, withdraws the member's name: a reader then shows the member as it would had they written none.

MemberProfileRecord.title: MemberProfileRecord

MemberProfileCleartext.title: MemberProfileCleartext
MemberProfileCleartext.description: A member's name on an `open` room: the `cleartext` of the `rooms/records/put` that writes the record (0.5 and later, which carry `kind`). The same rules as `MemberProfileRecord`, except that `body` is present and empty, because `cleartext` requires it, and that the record is not signed: on an `open` room the name is the writer's claim as the host stores it, attributed to the author the host recorded, like everything else there.
